alerts.reason: Curtiss-Wright reported a 2% sales decline as industrial gains only partly offset commercial aerospace weakness (A). Orders rose 11% (B), supporting a forecast that March-quarter sales stay above −5% year over year. Disruptions affecting both Curtiss-Wright and its suppliers (C) could delay shipments enough to push June-quarter sales to −5% or worse.

Activision segment net bookings fell $464 million as several titles generated fewer bookings than their comparators (B), while full-year consolidated revenue grew 9% (A). Deferred revenue on online-enabled products (C, D) could cushion the March quarter and delay the impact of weaker bookings, supporting a forecast of consolidated revenue growth above −5% in March and at or below −5% in June.

Higher industrial unit sales outside China had offset falling Chinese unit sales and lower average selling prices (D). That offset supports a forecast of March-quarter revenue growth above −5%. Customers delaying capital spending and implementation (B) could weaken unit sales outside China enough to push consolidated revenue growth to −5% or worse in June.
